English.question:
১) 1) Questions 1-40 : Read each sentence to find out whether there is any grammatical error or idiomatic error in it. If there is no error, choose ‘No error’.
We must regard any statement about this controversy, whatever the source, as gossip until they are confirmed.
English.exp: Error in pronoun-antecedent agreement. Replace ‘they are’ with ‘it is’.

English.question: 2) He is very senior to me, so I dare not disrespect him.
English.exp: Replace 'very' with 'much'. 'Very' should be used before Positive degree and 'much' should be used before Comparative degree. The correct sentence should be: He is much senior to me so I dare not disrespect him.

English.question: 3) ‘Pull it out by its plug, not by the cord,’ said dad.
English.exp:
Here, ‘Dad’ is a name or proper noun and should be capitalized. We are using 'Dad' like a name instead of saying ‘Mr. X’ (his name).
The word 'dad' can be capitalized depending on how it is used in a sentence or title. When used generically in a sentence such as: 'My dad is the best.', then the word ‘dad’ is lowercase because it is a generic noun.
However, if you are addressing your dad directly, such as: when asking a question, then you should capitalize the word ‘dad’. For instance, Can I go to the movies, Dad?

English.question: 4) Symptoms of this illness that warrant a doctor visit includes fever, vomiting, and diarrhea, as well as the loss of appetite.
English.option2: খ) that warrant a doctor visit
English.exp: 'Includes' is incorrect because it is the singular form of the verb, but the subject, 'symptoms,' is plural. The verb should be 'include.'

English.question: 5) Either Rahim or Karim forgot to take their pen.
English.exp: Replace ‘their’ with ‘his’. The correct sentence should be: Either Rahim or Karim forgot to take his pen.

English.question: 6) A free press is not a privilege but the organic necessity in a free society.
English.option1: ক) A free press is not
English.exp: Replace ‘the’ with ‘an’. The correct sentence should be: A free press is not a privilege but an organic necessity in a free society.

English.question: 7) Perspective visitors to tropical countries should plan to start taking antimalaria pills one or two weeks prior to their sitting out on their trips.
English.exp: Error in word usage. Perspective is a noun meaning viewpoint. Prospective is an adjective meaning expected or future. The visitors are prospective or future tourists. Replace ‘Perspective’ with ‘Prospective’.

English.question: 8) Whenever you speak take care that others are not offended by your words.
9) Asif prefers self-employment to job in any office.
English.exp: Use ‘a’ before ‘job’. ‘Job’ is a singular countable noun, hence, ‘a’ should be used. The correct sentence should be: Asif prefers self-employment to a job in any office.

English.question: 10) Scarcely had she gone when an inspector knocked at the door.
English.exp: বাক্যের শুরুতে scarcely, hardly, rarely, barely থাকলে inversion (auxiliary verb+subject+main verb) হয়। আর এই বাক্যটি scarcely…when এই Structure অনুযায়ী গঠিত হয়েছে।

English.question: 11) No sooner did the nurse enter the house then the patient died.
English.exp: Replace ‘then’ by ‘than’. The correct sentence should be: No sooner did the nurse enter the house than the patient died.

English.question: 12) We cannot handle this complicated case unless full details are not given to us.
English.option4: ঘ) are not given to us
English.exp: Remove ‘not’ after the word ‘are’. The correct sentence should be: We cannot handle this complicated case unless full details are given to us.

English.question: 13) The first portion of the book was dull, the later part was interesting.
English.option2: খ) of the book was dull,
English.exp: Latter points to the second, or last, of the two items in the sequence. The correct sentence should be:The first portion of the book was dull, the latter part was interesting.

English.question: 14) Either Lisa or Karen will always volunteer their valuable time to serve on our board.
English.option4: ঘ) time to serve on our board
English.exp: 'Their' is incorrect because it is a plural third-person possessive pronoun, but the use of 'either…or' indicates a singular form. It should be 'her.'

English.question: 15) The conversation with her mother had a more profound affect on her than she expected.
English.option1: ক) mother had a more profound
English.exp: The correct noun for this meaning is spelled 'effect.'

English.question: 16) The President and the Speaker of the House found the Congressional Republicans’ filibusters to be all together specious.
English.option2: খ) the Speaker of the House found
English.exp: This is incorrectly spelled as two words. In this sentence, it should be 'altogether,' a one-word adverb modifying the adjective 'specious' and meaning 'entirely' or 'completely.' 'All together' would be used for a different meaning, e.g. 'The family members were all together at the reunion.'

English.question: 17) They will put on a note in this regard for your consideration.
English.exp: Replace ‘on’ with ‘up’. The correct sentence should be: They will put up a note in this regard for your consideration.

English.question: 18) She knows very well what is expected from her but she is unable to perform.
English.option2: খ) what is expected from her
English.exp:
Replace ‘from’ with ‘of’. The correct expression should be ‘expected of her’. The correct sentence should be: She knows very well what is expected of her but she is unable to perform.
'Expected from' means that something, whether material or immaterial, is being anticipated to come from someone and that there will be an actual transfer of that something from the source to the one expecting it.
Eg : A negative response was expected from the manager.
'Expected of' means believing that someone is capable of living up to or adopting some standard of performance, behavior, or way of thinking.
Eg : It was expected of you to do a good job.

English.question: 19) Professor Lane, our Computer Science teacher, was excited when he had the opportunity to meet Bill Gates, the president of Microsoft, Inc.
20) 'They had went to the lake without me by the time I got there,' said Jacques.
English.option1: ক) had went to the lake
English.exp: The correct form for the past perfect tense of the irregular verb 'to go' is 'had gone,' not 'had went.' 'Went' is only used as the past tense, without the auxiliary 'had.'

English.question: 21) The top-ranking candidates will be appointed in senior jobs in Banks.
English.exp: Replace ‘in’ with ‘to’. The correct expression should be ‘appointed to’. The correct sentence should be: The top-ranking candidates will be appointed to senior jobs in Banks.

English.question: 22) Work as quick as you can but as carefully as possible when you take the test.
English.exp: The error is 'quick,' which is an adjective; here it should be the adverb 'quickly' instead, describing manner (how) to modify the verb 'Work.'

English.question: 23) Although the pain was behind his capacity, yet he didn’t complain.
English.exp: Replace ‘behind’ with ‘beyond’. ‘Beyond’ conveys at or more than the limit or threshold. The correct sentence should be: Although the pain was beyond his capacity, yet he didn’t complain.

English.question: 24) He freed himself from the burglar’s hold and ran on the road.
English.exp: Replace ‘on’ with ‘across’. The correct expression should be ‘across the road’. The correct sentence should be: He freed himself from the burglar’s hold and ran across the road.

English.question: 25) After opening the door we entered into the room next to the balcony.
English.exp: Remove ‘into’. The verb ‘enter’ does not take the preposition ‘into’. The correct expression should be ‘entered the room’. The correct sentence should be: After opening the door we entered the room next to the balcony.

English.question: 26) Children always quarrel above petty issues.
English.exp: Replace ‘above’ with ‘over’. Here, the correct preposition to be used should be ‘quarrel over’. The correct sentence should be: Children always quarrel over petty issues.

English.question: 27) A woman who always connives on the faults of her children is their worst enemy.
English.exp: Replace ‘on’ with ‘at’. The verb ‘connives’ takes the preposition ‘at’ after it. The correct sentence should be: A woman who always connives at the faults of her children is their worst enemy.

English.question: 28) Dr. Salam has been trying to develop a medicine for last five years.
English.exp: Replace ‘for’ with ‘since’. ‘For’ is used before a noun denoting a period of time with all the tenses. ‘Since’ is used before a noun or phrase denoting some point of time in the past. The correct sentence should be: Dr. Salam has been trying to develop a medicine since last five years.

English.question: 29) She was taken with surprise when she saw the famous Taj Mahal.
English.exp: Replace ‘with’ with ‘by’. The correct sentence should be: She was taken by surprise when she saw the famous Taj Mahal.

English.question: 30) His mentor, Abdur Rahman was blind within one eye.
English.exp: Replace ‘within’ with ‘in’. The correct expression should be ‘blind in one eye’ The correct sentence should be: His mentor, Abdur Rahman was blind in one eye.

English.question: 31) The rice is the favorite food of the Bengalis.
English.exp:
Remove ‘the’ before ‘rice’. Article is not used before the names of food-grains. The correct sentence should be: Rice is the favorite food of the Bengalis.
Note - If the name of the food-grain is attached with the name of a place or person, ‘the’ is used.
Example: The rice of Bangladesh is also exported to other countries.

English.question: 32) He has been promoted to the rank of the S.P.
English.exp: Remove ‘the’ before S.P.. Article is not used with the following phrases – kind of, type of, sort of, rank of, post of, title of etc. The correct sentence should be: He has been promoted to the rank of S.P.

English.question: 33) Neither the students nor the teacher were in his class.
English.exp: Replace 'were' with 'was'. When two different subjects are joined by 'either...or; neither...nor', the verb agrees with the subject near to it (generally second subject). Here, the verb is near to the second subject 'the teacher', it should agree with the second subject i.e. 'was' should be used. The correct sentence should be: Neither the students nor the teacher was in his class.

English.question: 34) It was by a mistake that he caught his hand.
English.exp:
Remove ‘a’ before ‘mistake’. The correct sentence should be: It was by mistake that he caught his hand.
Article should not be used before the following phrases-
By post, by chance, by mistake.

English.question: 35) The robbers were caught just before they were about to escape the jail.
English.exp: Remove ‘the’ before ‘jail’. Article should not be used before school, college, university, church, bed, hospital, prison, jail, court, bed, market, when these places are visited or used for their primary purpose. The correct sentence should be: The robbers were caught just before they were about to escape jail.

English.question: 36) He is not rich so he cannot afford to buy a expensive house.
English.exp: Replace ‘a’ with ‘an’. Before a word beginning with a vowel sound (A, E, I, O, U), ‘an’ should be used. The correct sentence should be: He is not rich so he cannot buy an expensive house.

English.question: 37) Amin’s habit of delaying his work put his friends to lot of trouble.
English.exp:
Use ‘a’ before ‘lot’. The correct sentence should be: Amin’s habit of delaying his work put his friends to a lot of trouble.
With the following expressions ‘a’ is used-
A lot (of), A great deal (of), A good deal (of), A large quantity (of), A large amount (of), A great many (of), A good many (of), A number (of), A large number of (of), A great number (of).

English.question: 38) Not only the principal but also the students was laughing.
English.exp: Replace 'was' with were'. When two subjects are joined by 'not only...but also', the verb must agree with the second subject. The correct sentence should be: Not only the principal but also the students were laughing.

English.question: 39) The manager as well as the clerks were fighting.
English.exp: Replace 'were' with 'was'. When two nouns are used with as well as, the verb must agree with the first subject. In this case, the first subject is 'manager', the correct verb to be used should be 'was'. The correct sentence should be: The manager as well as the clerks was fighting.

English.question: 40) The Elite class have no soft corner for the poor.
English.exp: Replace 'have' with 'has'. Collective nouns such as 'the elite class, the middle class etc' are treated as singular, so the verb should be 'singular'. The correct sentence should be: 'The Elite class has no soft corner for the poor.'

English.question: 41) Find the correctly spelt word.
English.exp: Itinerary- ভ্রমণপথ, ভ্রমণবৃত্তান্ত

English.question: 42) Find the correctly spelt word.
English.exp: Surveillance- নজরদারী

English.exp: Fahrenheit- তাপমান স্কেল

English.exp: Apparel- পোশাক

English.question: 45) Find the correctly spelt word.
English.exp: Renaissance- নবজাগরণ

English.question: 46) Find the correctly spelt word.
English.exp: Occurrence- ঘটনা

English.question: 47) Find the correctly spelt word.
English.exp: Inundated- প্লাবিত

English.question: 48) Find the correctly spelt word.
English.exp: Perseverance- অধ্যবসায়

English.question: 49) Find the correctly spelt word.
English.exp: Budgetary- আয়-ব্যয় সংক্রান্ত

English.question: 50) Find the correctly spelt word.
English.exp: Nuisance- উপদ্রব

English.question: 51) Find out the word which is wrongly spelt.
English.exp: Mischievious will be Mischievous. Mischievous is someone who tends to cause annoyance, trouble or minor injury.

English.question: 52) Find out the incorrect spelling.
English.exp: Conquerer will be Conqueror.

English.question: 53) Find out the incorrect spelling.
English.exp: Beaureaucracy will be Bureaucracy.

English.question: 54) Find out the incorrect spelling.
English.exp: Freshner will be Freshener.

English.question: 55) Find out the incorrect spelling.
English.exp: Refrendum will be Referendum.

English.question: 56) Find out the incorrect spelling.
English.exp: Eratic will be Erratic. Envelop means to wrap around something completely. But an envelope is a flat piece of paper used to enclose or envelop documents.

English.question: 57) Find out the incorrect spelling.
English.exp: Rejuvinate will be Rejuvenate.

English.question: 58) Find out the word which is wrongly spelt.
English.exp: Acquiescence- Acquiescence is an act of passive acceptance or submission.

English.question: 59) Find out the incorrect spelling.
English.exp: Concurence will be Concurrence.

English.question: 60) Find out the incorrect spelling.
English.exp: Couragous will be Courageous.

English.question: 61) The word ‘resolute’ is-
English.exp: resolute- অটল

English.question: 62) Which part of speech is the word ‘regarding’?
English.exp:
Example of ‘regarding’-
1. She has said nothing regarding your request.
2. Call me if you have any problems regarding your work.

English.question: 63) Which part of speech is the word ‘unless’?
English.exp:
as a conjunction (connecting two clauses): We won't go unless we're invited.
as a preposition (followed by a noun): There is no cure for his illness, unless an operation is performed.

English.question: 64) A barking dog seldom bites. Here, ‘barking’ does the function of-
English.exp: Here ‘barking’ is a Participle. Particple : verb+ing যদি adjective/verb এর কাজ করে (verbal adjective).

English.question: 65) In which sentence ‘after’ is used as a preposition?
English.option1: ক) After you’d left, I got a phone call from Stuart.
English.option2: খ) After that effort, everyone doubts whether she can win.
English.option3: গ) He died on June 3rd and was buried the day after.
English.option4: ঘ) After doing the task, I went to bed.
English.exp: Followed by a noun ‘after’ is used as a preposition.

English.question: 66) Which one is compound noun?
English.exp: Sometimes two or three nouns appear together, or even with other parts of speech, and create idiomatic compound nouns.

English.question: 67) What kind of noun is ‘Children’?
English.exp: A common noun is a name for something which is common for many things, person, or places. For instance, boy, girl, men, book etc.

English.question: 68) We need two hundred dollars ___ this to pay for everything.
English.exp: Besides refers to in addition to.

English.question: 69) His appearance is unsmiling but ___.
English.option2: খ) his heart is full of compassion for others.
English.option3: গ) people are afraid of him.
English.option4: ঘ) he is full of jealousy towards his colleagues.
English.exp: Conjunction ‘but’ adds two contrastive ideas.

English.question: 70) He did not study hard; ___ he passed the examination.
English.exp: Nevertheless is used when something bad is predicted but didn’t happen.

English.question: 71) The train was late. ___ I managed to arrive on time.
English.exp: Despite that- when something happened which was not expected to happen, we use despite that.

English.question: 72) ‘perhaps’ is-
English.exp:
It means maybe, possibly.
Example: Perhaps I will see you tomorrow.

English.question: 73) Down went the Titanic. Here, ‘Down’ is-
English.exp:
Down can be used in the following ways:
as a preposition (followed by a noun): She was walking down the street.
as an adverb (without a following noun): She lay down and fell asleep.
after the verb ‘to be’: Oil prices are down.
as an adjective: I’ve been feeling rather down lately.
In this question, without a following noun 'Down' is used as an adverb.

English.question: 74) I find it very unlikely. Here, ‘unlikely’ is-
75) Hand me that cricket bat. Here ‘that’ is-
English.exp: Demonstrative pronouns normally indicate the closeness of or distance from the speaker, either literally or symbolically. This, these, that, and those are the demonstrative pronouns. They also work as demonstrative adjectives when they modify a noun. However, demonstrative pronouns do not modify anything rather replace the nouns/noun phrases. Demonstrative adjectives include the words: this, that, these, those. In this question, 'that' modifies the noun 'cricket bat'. So, it's a demonstrative adjective.

English.question: ৭৬) Credit tk 4000 ___ my account.
English.exp: To deposit an amount to someone’s account, we use credit to.

English.question: 77) She feels ____ scared.
English.exp: Both these words, ‘so’ and ‘extremely’ are adverbs of degree which modifies the adjective ‘scared’.

English.question: 78) Which one is a countable noun?
79) not only-but also, either-or, neither-nor, both-and, whether-or etc. are-
80) I explained him everything lest he ___ misunderstand me.
English.exp: Subject+verb+....+lest+Subject+should/might+verb+extension
